title: Add spire-tpm-plugin support to spire NixOS module
reason: Applicable: real spire-agent module + wired test. Real diff adds a new TPM NodeAttestor plugin option in a NEW file (agent-tpm.nix) not included as this target's own `module`; watched a pre-existing, unchanged field (trust_domain) in the main agent.nix instead, to probe a real doubly-repeated path-segment shape (services.spire.agent.settings.agent.trust_domain -- 'agent' appears twice).
targets_toml: single target spire-agent, module=agent.nix only (agent-tpm.nix, where the PR's own real new content lives, was not included as the module target given oba takes one module path -- the new TPM option itself was not directly probed this pass), cfg_ident=cfg, option_prefix=[services,spire,agent,settings,agent] (the full real absolute path, confirmed via an initial shallower-prefix run whose discovered_options listed ['settings','agent','trust_domain'] relative to [services,spire,agent]), watch=[trust_domain].

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.note: GENUINELY CONFUSING RESULT worth flagging with care: a shallower option_prefix=[services,spire,agent] run showed trust_domain present in discovered_options (as a 3-segment relative path ['settings','agent','trust_domain'], implying the full absolute path is services.spire.agent.settings.agent.trust_domain -- note 'agent' appears twice, once as the top-level cfg namespace and once as a real nested settings key). But re-running with the FULL matching option_prefix=[services,spire,agent,settings,agent] returns EMPTY discovered_options and OptionNotFound for the watched option -- the deeper, more-specific prefix found LESS than the shallower one, which is the opposite of what I'd expect. Possibly a real resolution bug specific to a path with a repeated segment name; possibly a real limitation in how I'm allowed to specify option_prefix at all. Not confirmed either way, flagging as a third, structurally distinct candidate_capability_gap shape from the mkPackageOption and dotted-path-blackout ones.
